definitions.explanation: An object that someone has found lying on the ground or left behind. Used for items found by chance.
Something unexpectedly good that one comes across by luck. Used figuratively for bargains, surprisingly talented people, or fortunate discoveries.

examples.japanese: {拾|ひろ}い{物|もの}は{交番|こうばん}に{届|とど}けよう。
examples.english: Let's turn in found items at the police box.

examples.japanese: {道|みち}で{拾|ひろ}い{物|もの}をしたら、{警察|けいさつ}に{届|とど}ける{義務|ぎむ}がある。
examples.english: If you find something on the street, you have an obligation to report it to the police.

examples.japanese: この{財布|さいふ}は{拾|ひろ}い{物|もの}ですので、{持|も}ち{主|ぬし}を{探|さが}しています。
examples.english: This wallet was found, so we are looking for its owner.

examples.japanese: このセールは{拾|ひろ}い{物|もの}だった。
examples.english: This sale was a real find.

examples.japanese: {無名|むめい}の{選手|せんしゅ}だったが、{今|いま}シーズンは{拾|ひろ}い{物|もの}と{言|い}える{活躍|かつやく}だ。
examples.english: He was an unknown player, but his performance this season can be called a real find.

examples.japanese: {古本屋|ふるほんや}で{見|み}つけた{初版本|しょはんぼん}は、{思|おも}いがけない{拾|ひろ}い{物|もの}だった。
examples.english: The first edition I found at the used bookstore was an unexpected windfall.

notes:
USAGE:
Sense 1 (literal found object) is common in everyday and legal contexts. Japan has a strong culture of turning in found items, and {拾|ひろ}い{物|もの} is the standard term used at police boxes and lost-and-found offices.

Sense 2 (figurative windfall) is commonly used in sports, shopping, and entertainment contexts to describe surprisingly good discoveries.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {拾|ひろ}い{物|もの}をする (find/pick up something)
- {拾|ひろ}い{物|もの}を{届|とど}ける (turn in a found item)
- {思|おも}わぬ{拾|ひろ}い{物|もの} (unexpected find)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {落|お}とし{物|もの}: lost item — the perspective of the person who lost it
- {掘|ほ}り{出|だ}し{物|もの}: bargain, treasure find — specifically a valuable item found at a low price
